subject: Daggerford
fact: Daggerford has walls, a market square, smoke from cook fires, and the smell of horses.
source_quote: Daggerford was the first place we'd walked into in weeks where the silence didn't make sense. Daggerford had people. Daggerford had walls, and a market square, and smoke from cook fires, and the smell of horses.

subject: bronze-cast forearm
fact: A bronze-cast forearm, severed at the elbow, mounted on a stone pillar, not holding anything.
source_quote: There was a monument there — a bronze-cast forearm, severed at the elbow, mounted on a stone pillar. Not holding anything. Just a hand.

subject: Tarvis Ulain
fact: Tarvis Ulain, paladin, dead three years, died in Daggerford breaking up a Cult of the Dragon recruitment operation.
source_quote: The primary text told us this was Tarvis Ulain, paladin, dead three years. Died here, in Daggerford itself, breaking up a Cult of the Dragon recruitment operation.

subject: Dwarven inscription
fact: The Dwarven inscription on the base reads: 'The move is yours.'
source_quote: There was a smaller inscription on the base. Dwarven, on the base. *The move is yours.*

subject: Common inscription
fact: The Common inscription on the back reads: 'Witnessed and recorded for the Gauntlet.' Signed by Milo Goodbarrel.
source_quote: There was a smaller inscription on the back. Common. *Witnessed and recorded for the Gauntlet.* Signed by Milo Goodbarrel, apparently head of some publisher, apparently Order of the Gauntlet.

subject: Metalworkers Guild
fact: The Metalworkers Guild funded the monument two years after the war.
source_quote: The whole thing was funded two years after the war by a Metalworkers Guild.

subject: pewter hand casts
fact: Small pewter reproductions of Tarvis's hand cast, charm-sized, sold for donations to the Order of the Gauntlet.
source_quote: A village priest caught us in the doorway — walking in very pleased with himself and carrying a tray of small pewter reproductions of Tarvis's hand cast, miniature things, charm-sized. He was selling them for donations to the Order of the Gauntlet.

subject: Milo Goodbarrel
fact: Milo Goodbarrel, head of a publisher and member of the Order of the Gauntlet, personally signed the monument's inscription.
source_quote: Signed by Milo Goodbarrel, apparently head of some publisher, apparently Order of the Gauntlet. Milo had personally signed off on this.

subject: River Shining Tavern
fact: The River Shining Tavern is where the group paused before entering, after noting the monument.
source_quote: We found the River Shining Tavern and noted it for later. But we didn't go straight in...

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum dropped a gold piece for a pewter hand cast and asked the priest why the Stroudite inscription remained on a Bahamutian paladin's monument.
source_quote: Grygum dropped a gold piece in for his. Then Grygum asked him to tell him more — he'd already paid, so he had the leverage — and the priest was very willing. 'The inscription shares language with Stroud. Why is that?'

subject: Priest of Bahamut
fact: The priest claimed to be a pure Bahamutian and conceded the inscription was a gift left in place because Tarvis saved everyone regardless of the chess game.
source_quote: He himself was, he wanted us to know, *a pure Bahamutian*. He did not believe in the heresy. 'It was a gift,' he said finally. 'And since it was a gift, we decided the inscription could remain. After all — wasn't Tarvis trying to save us all, regardless of what actually happened in that game of chess?'

subject: Maerith of the Ford
fact: Maerith of the Ford is the home of Elin, a 7-year-old girl who has been silent for six days and draws a six-pointed star on every flat surface.
source_quote: Maerith of the Ford had the look of a woman who had already been turned away... 'My daughter Elin is 7 years old and has been silent for 6 days. She draws the same shape on every flat surface. She talks in her sleep.'

subject: six-pointed star
fact: Elin draws a six-pointed star over and over on every flat surface in her home.
source_quote: Yes, she'd noted the drawings — a six-pointed star, over and over, every flat surface in the house.

subject: Elin
fact: Elin spoke after Lesser Restoration: 'The wells are not wells anymore.'
source_quote: And then she spoke. 'The wells are not wells anymore.'

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer, the sentient sword, performed Lesser Restoration on Elin, enabling her speech.
source_quote: Dawnbringer could help. Dawnbringer did not wait for a second invitation. 'Let me bring the light to you.' Lesser restoration settled in.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz has been experiencing pressure in his head, possibly linked to the same phenomenon affecting Elin.
source_quote: Daz mentioned the pressure in his own head — had been mentioning it, in various indirect ways, for a while now.

subject: The Burning Wizard Inn
fact: The Burning Wizard Inn is named for a wizard burned alive by a dragon cult decades prior, and the south wall still bears the memory of his death.
source_quote: The Burning Wizard Inn took its name from a death. That was the first thing I catalogued... 'That is where he fell. We scrub the floor every season. We do not paint over the wall. My grandfather said the wall remembers.'

subject: Festrum
fact: Festrum, the gnome innkeeper, has maintained the Burning Wizard Inn for thirty years and remembers the story of the burned wizard.
source_quote: Festrum — the gnome innkeeper, old enough to have heard the story from the people who told it first — pointed to the south wall without prompting...

subject: The Kenku Could Not Fly
fact: The bard's song 'The Kenku Could Not Fly' includes the lyric: 'The raven thief who learned to steal no more, save what was needed.'
source_quote: This one was called 'The Kenku Could Not Fly.'... 'The raven thief who learned to steal no more, save what was needed, said the small, wise man at his side.'

subject: Whistler
fact: Whistler, the Kenku thief, took only what was necessary from Tiamat’s hoard, forming a line-item budget.
source_quote: The Kenku thief of some earlier age who, presented with the complete hoard of Tiamat, had apparently taken only what was necessary for legitimate expenses. Operating goals. Day-to-day funds. Per diems.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum observed that Whistler’s restraint mapped well onto his own philosophy.
source_quote: Grygum, who has an irritating habit of noticing things I would have preferred to notice first, observed drily that the song's principle — steal what was needed — mapped rather well onto Whistler.
